id.description: Unique within the corpus; a runner reports failures by it.

dialect.description: Id of the dialect to parse `input` with. Always explicit here: detection is a parse-case concern.

input.description: The expression exactly as a user would type it.

timezone.description: IANA zone name the schedule runs in.

from.description: RunOptions.from, exclusive: a run exactly at `from` is not returned, since no case sets `inclusive`.

until.description: RunOptions.until, inclusive: a run exactly at `until` is returned.

anchor.description: RunOptions.anchor for an interval schedule. When absent, next() is called without one, so the anchor defaults to `from`; the derived checks then pass `from` as the anchor explicitly.

count.description: RunOptions.count. `expect` may hold fewer runs than this (the schedule ran out, or until/the horizon cut it off), never more.

expect.description: Exactly what next(schedule, {from, count, until}) returns, in order. Instants are non-decreasing; equal instants occur only in a group that begins with skipped-adjusted runs.

local.description: Run.local: the run's wall time in the schedule timezone with its UTC offset. The seconds of the offset appear only when it has any (historical LMT offsets).

dst.description: How this run relates to a UTC-offset transition. Absent when the run's wall time is unambiguous and really occurred.

scheduled.description: Only on a skipped-adjusted run: the wall time the run is catching up, which the gap skipped. It carries no offset because that wall time does not exist in the zone. Runs sharing an instant are told apart by this field.

notMatching.description: Instants a runner must assert matches() is false for: the cases where a plain wall-clock field test would say true but the dialect's DST strategy does not emit the run.

skipDerived.description: Suppresses the derived matches() and prev() checks (see corpus/README.md). For a case whose `expect` is deliberately a partial view of its window.

provenance.description: Where the expected values come from. `spec` = the dialect specification or documented behaviour; `derived` = read from reference source, with `source` citing the section; `assumed` = the platform's documentation is silent and this is the behaviour the corpus chose; `source` cites the DERIVATION entry that records the silence and the reason; `captured` = recorded from a running reference implementation, with `platform` and `recording`.

instant.description: An absolute instant, always UTC and always whole seconds.
